newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL'S CEMIG H1 NET FALLS VS YEAR AGO.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL'S CEMIG H1 NET FALLS VS YEAR AGO.

text.p: Brazilian power company Companhia Energetica de Minas Gerais (Cemig), owned by Minas Gerais state, reported the following first-half 1997 results.
NOTE: Figures are in Brazilian reais and are not adjusted for inflation.
In a statement, Cemig said net profit fell 23.5 percent compared with the January-June period last year. It said ajusted net profit reached 145 million reais, down 7.4 percent from 1996's first half.

Cemig's Financial Director Francisco Luiz Penna was quoted as saying non-adjusted net revenues rose 125.1 million reais against the 1996's first half due to rising operating expenses, mainly from power purchases from Itaipu dam, which are in dollars and subject to exchange rate fluctuations.
The April rise in rates was not enough to offset the increased expenses, he said.
Even so, "Cemig continues to have an operating cost of 45 reais per megawatt-hour (MWh), the lowest among the large Brazilian concessionaires," Penna was quoted as saying.

April's rate increase helped second quarter results, which showed a 62.3 million real net profit, a 133 percent rise from 26.7 million reais in the first quarter, the statement said. Second quarter net receipts reached 549 million reais against 484 million reais in January-March.

Penna said electrical energy sales reached 19.2 million MWh in the first half, up 4.7 percent versus the same period last year. "Cemig's projection was for four percent growth this year," he was quoted as saying.

The company cut its payroll to 14,631 by June 30, 1997, down 5.1 percent from the end of 1996's first half. Cemig's debt totalled 1.048 billion reais, 11.7 percent of its net worth in the first half, and 59 percent of its debt was in denominated in a foreign currency.
